pathways.name: Type I Interferon Signature
pathways.description: The IFN signature is the dominant molecular hallmark of SS — present in ~60-70% of patients. Salivary gland plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) produce IFN-α in response to immune complexes containing anti-Ro/SSA autoantibodies and RNA, engaging TLR7. The IFN signature score correlates with disease activity, anti-Ro/SSA titers, hypergammaglobulinemia, and lymphoma risk. IRF5 and STAT4 are key genetic drivers of this pathway in SS.

pathways.name: B Cell Hyperactivity & BAFF/APRIL Signaling
pathways.description: B cell hyperactivity is the hallmark immunologic feature of SS. BAFF (BLyS/TNFSF13B) is markedly elevated in serum, saliva, and salivary glands, driving survival and differentiation of autoreactive B cells. BAFF-R, TACI, and BCMA are the three BAFF/APRIL receptors on B cells. Transgenic BAFF overexpression in mice recapitulates SS-like disease including salivary gland destruction and lymphoma. The BAFF pathway directly links B cell hyperactivity to the ~15-20× increased risk of marginal zone B cell lymphoma in SS.

pathways.name: Tfh-Germinal Center Axis & Lymphoid Neogenesis
pathways.description: SS salivary glands are a site of active germinal center (GC) formation — ectopic lymphoid structures with B cell follicles, Tfh cells, and follicular dendritic cell networks. GC+ salivary gland biopsies are associated with higher disease activity, more severe glandular destruction, and increased lymphoma risk. The CXCL13-CXCR5 axis directs Tfh and B cells to these follicles. CD40-CD40L costimulation drives GC reactions. This GC biology is directly targetable via CD40 blockade (iscalimab) and BAFF inhibition.
therapeutic_targets: abatacept (CTLA4-Ig — indirect T cell costimulation block)

pathways.name: TLR7/9 Innate Immune Sensing
pathways.description: TLR7 (ssRNA sensor) and TLR9 (unmethylated CpG DNA sensor) in endosomes of pDCs and B cells drive IFN-α production and B cell activation in SS. Anti-Ro/SSA antibodies form immune complexes with RNA-containing autoantigens, which are endocytosed via FcγRIIa (FCGR2A) and delivered to TLR7-containing endosomes. This creates a self-amplifying loop: immune complexes → pDC activation → IFN-α → B cell activation → more autoantibodies → more immune complexes. Hydroxychloroquine inhibits this pathway by preventing endosomal acidification required for TLR activation.

pathways.name: JAK-STAT Signaling in SS
pathways.description: Multiple cytokines driving SS pathology signal through JAK-STAT pathways: type I IFN (JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/2), IL-6 (JAK1/JAK2 → STAT3), IL-12/23 (TYK2/JAK2 → STAT4), and IL-21 (JAK1/JAK3 → STAT3). STAT4 is a major SS genetic risk factor. JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib) are being investigated in SS, with early case series showing improvement in systemic disease and glandular function.

pathways.name: NF-κB / Inflammatory Cytokine Axis
pathways.description: Chronic NF-κB activation drives IL-6, TNF-α, and BAFF production. TNFAIP3/TNIP1 dysfunction leads to persistent NF-κB in salivary glands.

pathways.name: Tissue Remodeling, Fibrosis & Lymphoma
pathways.description: Chronic inflammation leads to gland destruction, fibrosis, and 15-20x lymphoma risk.
